title: Can you solve this puzzle quiz? (Puzzle + Roguelike)
author: orangeun22
selftext:
I'm currently working on a **demo** for a puzzle-roguelike game on Steam, and I'd love to get your thoughts on how the puzzle difficulty feels.



Quick overview: On an N×N board, there are color-coded hint blocks where each color represents a monster, trap, treasure, or event. The goal of the quiz is to pinpoint the exact location of the yellow treasure block. None of the hint blocks rotate or flip, and there is only one unique solution.



https://i.redd.it/j8hxz16gcd4i1.png



Did you find the yellow treasure block? 

Here's a harder one.



https://i.redd.it/titldylgcd4i1.png



I'd really appreciate any feedback on how tough these puzzles are. A demo is coming soon, so if this looks interesting to you, feel free to check out the Steam page: ROGRID

For context, this isn't just a standalone deduction puzzle—the game builds a full **roguelike** around this core rule. The core mechanic is inspired by Minesweeper, since I love both deduction puzzles and roguelikes. By deducing the colors of the hint blocks, you hunt down monsters, earn rewards, level up, and unlock skills. You can combine items and artifacts to push deeper, dodge traps, and run into events that grant buffs or strange situations. Managing your HP and action points forces tough choices between hunting more monsters or descending to the next floor, alongside multiple classes and upgrades.



There have been plenty of games that simply mash Minesweeper with roguelikes, but I haven't seen one built around block deduction like this before. 

Any feedback is always welcome, and thanks for checking it out!



\----

  
We utilized generative AI to create the artwork and sound for ROGRID, as well as to handle localization and translation tasks. How do you all maintain UI and visual consistency? That seems to be the most challenging aspect when working with AI.
